issues.legal_issue: A perfected pre-emption decree is not barred from supporting a claim to the land on the ground that the right or decree is purely personal.
material_facts: A pre-emption decree was made in favour of the original pre-emptor, who deposited the amounts required by the decree and thereby perfected title to the land.
An earlier decision between the same parties had held that the statutory right of pre-emption attaches to the land and that the pre-emptor's legal representatives could continue the proceedings.
The respondents argued that the decree was personal and could not support the subsequent purchasers’ claim.
issues.conclusion: The earlier inter partes decision settled the issue, so the contention that the decree was personal and created no interest in the land could not be reopened and failed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle stated in Hazari & Ors. v. Neki & Ors., the statutory right of pre-emption is not merely a personal right: it attaches to the land and may be enforced against a purchaser, although it is not itself an interest in the land. A determination between the same parties is binding in later proceedings between them.

predicates.preemption_decree_execution_case: The proceeding concerns execution of a decree made in a pre-emption action.
predicates.prior_inter_partes_ruling_on_preemption_: An earlier decision between the same parties determined the legal character of the pre-emption right.
predicates.decree_conditions_fulfilled: The pre-emptor complied with the conditions imposed by the decree.

issues.definition: When execution concerns a pre-emption decree whose conditions were fulfilled and an earlier decision between the same parties determined the character of the right, the objection that the right is purely personal is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser of land from a pre-emptor who perfected title under a decree may execute that decree for possession as a person claiming under the decree-holder, even when the decree itself was not assigned.
material_facts: The pre-emptor complied with the payment conditions in the decrees, thereby perfecting title to the land.
After perfecting title, the pre-emptor sold the land to the appellants, but the sale deed did not assign the decrees.
The appellants sought possession by executing the decrees, and the pre-emptor could himself have applied to execute them.
The lower appellate court held the applications maintainable, while the High Court rejected them.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were persons claiming under the decree-holder and could maintain the execution applications under section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the appeals were allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a person claiming under someone who could take a proceeding or make an application to do so, unless the Code otherwise provides. Order XXI, rule 16 applies where a decree is transferred by assignment in writing or by operation of law; failure to establish such an assignment does not itself prevent recourse to section 146. Jugal Kishore Saraf v. Raw Cotton Co. Ltd. supports that distinction, and Smt. Saila Bala Dassi v. Smt. Nirmala Sundari Dassi supports a liberal construction of section 146 to advance justice.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and decree_for_possession_in_preemption_case and decree_conditions_fulfilled and title_perfected_before_land_transfer and land_transferred_to_applicant and not decree_assigned and original_decree_holder_could_execute

predicates.execution_proceeding: The applicant seeks to obtain possession through execution of a decree.
predicates.decree_for_possession_in_preemption_case: The decree sought to be executed grants possession following a pre-emption action.
predicates.decree_conditions_fulfilled: The pre-emptor complied with the conditions imposed by the decree.
predicates.title_perfected_before_land_transfer: The pre-emptor perfected title to the land before transferring it.
predicates.land_transferred_to_applicant: The decree-holder transferred the land to the execution applicant.
predicates.decree_assigned: The decree-holder transferred the decree itself to the applicant by assignment in writing or by operation of law.
predicates.original_decree_holder_could_execute: The original decree-holder was entitled to apply to execute the decree.

issues.definition: If a person seeking possession in execution bought land from a pre-emptor after the pre-emptor fulfilled the decree’s conditions and perfected title, and the decree-holder could have executed the decree, the purchaser may execute it as a person claiming under the decree-holder even if the decree itself was not assigned.
